title: The Roses in the Vineyard
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, and local investigator Detective Momoi, who functions the same as a recurring police interrogator) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Old cases/ep695 file got the culprit right (Yurika Suwayama) but was far thinner than the transcript supports: it collapsed three physically distinct ropes (hand/feet ties, the neck-to-ankle murder rig, and the reef-knot rope used to stage the hanging) into a single object, omitted the Mizumachi red-herring arc entirely (he confined Kengo at Yurika's request but did not kill him -- Momoi initially accuses him), omitted witnesses Shuuji Takashina and Akihiro Yamaguchi, and collapsed the case's actual solving mechanism -- the contrast between the northern field's acidic pyroligneous-acid pesticide (which darkens silver and reddens the yellow roses there) and the southern field's alkaline Bordeaux mixture (which does neither) -- into one vague 'pesticide fumes' clue. That north/south chemical contrast, not just 'mud on shoes', is what actually breaks both Mizumachi's and then Yurika's alibi claims. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Kengo's hand/foot ropes use two half-hitches (an agricultural knot); the rope that hung him from the stake uses a plain reef knot -- two different people tied them, ruling out a single lone actor.

Litmus paper touched to Mizumachi's clothes stays blue instead of turning pink, proving he was never exposed to the pyroligneous acid sprayed 1-4pm in the north field, so he never re-entered the barrel-cellar area during the death window.

Yurika's silver hairpin oxidized black, which only the north field's acidic pyroligneous-acid spray causes; the south field's alkaline Bordeaux mixture leaves silver and the yellow roses there unchanged -- so she lied about spending that time in the south field.
Straight, unresisting toe-drag marks matching Kengo's shoes show his face-down body was dragged to the wall already dead, contradicting the scene staged to look like he was hanged there alive.

business_survival_pressure (red herring; wanted the contract to succeed, confined Kengo for Yurika's sake, but did not kill him -- wrongly accused for lacking an alibi)
